title: Add to a Range

concept.title: The difference array
body: Adding a value `v` to every element of a range `[l, r]` one by one costs O(n) per update. A **difference array** `d` makes it O(1): put `+v` at `d[l]` and `-v` at `d[r + 1]`. The real values are the running sums of `d`: the `+v` starts to count at `l` and is cancelled by the `-v` after `r`.

body.code:
d = [0] * (n + 2)
for l, r, v in updates:
    d[l] += v
    d[r + 1] -= v
cur = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    cur += d[i]      # value of position i
    result.append(cur)

body: This is the reverse of prefix sums: prefix sums answer many range *queries* after one preparation; the difference array applies many range *updates* before one final pass.

statement: An array of `n` zeros is given (positions 1 to n). Then `q` updates follow. Each update gives `l`, `r` and `v` and adds `v` to every position from `l` to `r`. Print the final array.
inputFormat: Each of the next `q` lines has `l`, `r` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print the `n` final values on one line.
hints: Changing a whole range one position at a time is too slow for many updates.
Add `v` at position `l` and subtract `v` at position `r + 1` in a helper array.
Finally, the value of position `i` is the sum of the helper array up to `i`.

explanation: Each update touches only two cells of the difference array. One prefix-sum pass at the end turns the differences into the real values.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
u = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

d = [0] * (n + 2)
for l, rr, v in u:
    d[l] += v
    d[rr + 1] -= v
cur = 0
out = []
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    cur += d[i]
    out.append(cur)
print(*out)
